page_hint: §3, 'When to Disaggregate: Prefill and Decode Want Different Pools'
quoted_clause: prefill is **compute-bound** — compute-dominated there, a regime statement not a law (Ch 2) (~1.29 PFLOP → ~1.19 PFLOPS required over the ~1.08 s prefill budget, vs 0.989 PFLOPS peak on a single H100; under the canonical 8xH100 TP=8 host the same prefill is ~0.16 PFLOP per GPU and takes ~0.47 s at 35% MFU (Ch 12), so the single-device figure describes a one-GPU deployment, not the canonical host), decode is **bandwidth-bound** (arithmetic intensity = B FLOP/byte for FP16 weights: ~1.0 at batch 1, ~17.5 at the canonical ~17.5-concurrent operating point (Ch 4 §6 / Ch 7 / Ch 17; 436 GB ÷ 24.9 GB = KV budget ÷ per-request KV) — both far below the H100 ridge of ~295 FLOP/byte, so bandwidth binds; the whole-model weight-read rate is ~5.6 TB/s if served by one device vs 3.35 TB/s per GPU, sharded to ~0.70 TB/s per GPU under the canonical 8×H100 host, Ch 6)
observed: A single ~150-word sentence contains four or more levels of nested parentheticals carrying two independent derivations (prefill FLOP budget and decode arithmetic-intensity/weight-read-rate), six cross-references, and two regime qualifications. The reader must hold the main claim (prefill compute-bound, decode bandwidth-bound) in working memory while parsing deeply nested derivations and qualifications.
correction: Restructure into: (1) a short topic sentence stating both regime claims with the Ch 2 qualification; (2) a prefill derivation sentence or two; (3) a decode derivation sentence or two. Keep cross-references but reduce nesting to at most one level per sentence. Example skeleton: 'At the canonical operating point, prefill is compute-bound and decode is bandwidth-bound — both regime statements, not laws (Ch 2). Prefill: ~1.29 PFLOP over the ~1.08 s budget requires ~1.19 PFLOPS, above a single H100's 0.989 PFLOPS peak; on the canonical 8×H100 TP=8 host the per-GPU share is ~0.16 PFLOP, completed in ~0.47 s at 35% MFU (Ch 12). Decode: weight-read arithmetic intensity is B FLOP/byte for FP16 — ~1.0 at batch 1, ~17.5 at the canonical ~17.5-concurrent operating point (436 GB ÷ 24.9 GB; Ch 4 §6 / Ch 7 / Ch 17) — both far below the H100 ridge of ~295 FLOP/byte, so bandwidth binds. The whole-model weight-read rate is ~5.6 TB/s at batch 1 (Ch 6), sharded to ~0.70 TB/s per GPU on the canonical host.'
acceptance_test: The restructured passage contains no sentence with more than two levels of parenthetical nesting; all numerical values and cross-references are preserved; a reader can identify both regime claims and both derivations within one pass.
verdict_evidence: chapter-11.md §3 'When to Disaggregate': the paragraph from 'prefill is **compute-bound**' to '...not a law (Ch 2) [1P][DERIVED]' is a single 308-word sentence carrying 7 cross-references (Ch 2, Ch 4 §6, Ch 6, Ch 7, Ch 12, Ch 17) and nested parentheses two levels deep; its arithmetic checks out (1.29/1.08 ≈ 1.19 PFLOPS; 1.29/8 = 0.161 PFLOP; 0.161 ÷ (0.989×0.35) ≈ 0.47 s; 436 ÷ 24.9 = 17.5; 140 GB ÷ 25 ms = 5.6 TB/s; 140/8 GB ÷ 25 ms = 0.70 TB/s; 989 ÷ 3.35 ≈ 295 FLOP/byte), so the defect is load, not numbers.
fix_instruction: Split the §3 paragraph into: (1) a short topic sentence giving both regime claims with the Ch 2 'not a law' qualification; (2) a prefill derivation sentence or two; (3) a decode derivation sentence or two; keep the cross-references but keep nesting to at most one level per sentence.

quoted_clause: | Technique | Mechanism | Primary resource traded | When it matters | Source |
observed: The column header 'Primary resource traded' does not accurately describe the column content for all rows. For PagedAttention ('memory capacity') and prefix caching ('prefill FLOPs + memory') a genuine trade is described. For continuous batching ('compute+bandwidth util') the entry describes a resource whose utilization improves, not something traded away. For discrete batching ('slot occupancy (wastes capacity)') the entry describes waste, not a trade. For P/D disaggregation ('both at scale') the entry is ambiguous about what is given up.
correction: Rename the column to 'Primary resource lever' or 'Resource affected', which accurately covers all five rows: discrete batching wastes slot occupancy; continuous batching leverages compute+bandwidth utilization; PagedAttention leverages memory capacity; prefix caching leverages prefill FLOPs and memory; P/D disaggregation leverages both at scale. Alternatively, keep 'traded' and rewrite the continuous-batching and discrete-batching entries to describe an actual trade (e.g., continuous batching: 'scheduling complexity for utilization').
acceptance_test: Every row's entry in the renamed column accurately describes what the header claims, without requiring the reader to reinterpret the header per row.
verdict_evidence: chapter-11.md Table 11-1 header 'Primary resource traded' over rows 'slot occupancy (wastes capacity)', 'compute+bandwidth util', 'memory capacity', 'prefill FLOPs + memory', 'both at scale' — the column mixes resources wasted, resources leveraged, and (for P/D disaggregation) no resource at all ('both at scale'), so the header's give-up/get semantics does not describe the cells; Table 10-1 uses the safer header 'Communicates' for the same idea.
fix_instruction: Rename the Table 11-1 column to 'Primary resource lever' or 'Resource affected' (or split into 'Resource affected' and 'Whether capacity is gained or wasted') so all five rows — including 'both at scale' — are accurately described.

quoted_clause: The batch is locked until its *slowest* member finishes (fits-all-in-one-run)
observed: The parenthetical '(fits-all-in-one-run)' is awkward compound-adjective phrasing that is not standard terminology and could confuse readers. It appears to mean 'all requests fit in one run/batch' but the hyphenation makes it read as a single compound modifier.
correction: Replace with a standard phrase: '(the batch runs to completion)' or simply remove the parenthetical, since the preceding clause 'locked until its slowest member finishes' already conveys the meaning.
acceptance_test: The parenthetical is either removed or replaced with a standard, self-explanatory phrase.
verdict_evidence: chapter-11.md §3 'Discrete Batching Wastes the GPU': 'The batch is locked until its *slowest* member finishes (fits-all-in-one-run)' — the parenthetical 'fits-all-in-one-run' occurs exactly once in the chapter, is not standard terminology, and restates in hyphenated form what the preceding clause already says; the book's own wording elsewhere is 'runs them to completion' / 'runs each batch to completion'.
fix_instruction: Drop the parenthetical or replace it with the book's standard phrase, e.g. 'The batch is locked until its *slowest* member finishes (the batch runs to completion)'.

quoted_clause: The four are independent dials — mechanisms can be combined in principle, subject to implementation support and resource interactions
observed: The word 'independent' in 'independent dials' suggests the four mechanisms do not affect each other, but the immediately following clause acknowledges 'resource interactions' (e.g., prefix caching and continuous batching drawing on the same KV pool). The figure title uses 'separable concerns, not a stack' — 'separable' is the more accurate term (addressable in any order) while 'independent' overstates the claim.
correction: Change 'independent dials' to 'separable dials' or 'independently addressable dials' to match the figure title and the acknowledged resource interactions.
acceptance_test: The figure description uses 'separable' or an equivalent term consistent with the figure title and the acknowledged interactions.
verdict_evidence: chapter-11.md Fig 11.2 legend: the figure title says 'Serving is four separable concerns, not a stack (they interact — batching pressure feeds KV residency — but each is addressable in any order)' while the same legend then says 'The four are independent dials — mechanisms can be combined in principle, subject to implementation support and resource interactions (e.g. prefix caching under aggressive continuous batching: cached prefixes and the live batch's pages draw on the same 640 GB KV pool...)' — 'independent' contradicts the figure's own 'separable'/'they interact' wording.
fix_instruction: Change 'The four are independent dials' to 'The four are separable dials' (or 'independently addressable dials') in the Fig 11.2 legend so it matches the figure title and the acknowledged resource interactions.

observed: The green encoding is given two different semantics on the same page: the legend defines green as 'admission event (backfill)' (an instant), while the in-figure annotation under the continuous panel reads 'new sequences (green) snap into free slots' (a duration — a sequence occupying the slot). The drawn green strips have nonzero width, i.e., they depict admitted sequences in flight, not point events.
acceptance_test: Legend label and in-figure annotation assign the same referent to green (e.g., legend reads 'newly admitted sequence (backfill)'), or the strips are redrawn as zero-width markers consistent with 'event'. Re-render and confirm both labels match.
verdict_evidence: p.207 (P2 variant, Qwen): right-panel rows read [blue][thin green hatched tick][blue][thin green tick][blue], confirming green is an admission tick and not the sequence; the bottom annotation still calls the green 'new sequences', so a reader can take the tick for the sequence's decode.
fix_instruction: Reword the bottom annotation to 'a freed slot is backfilled at the green admission tick; the new sequence then runs as the following blue block', so no reading makes the green tick the sequence itself.

observed: Border style varies across the four boxes (1 solid, 2 dotted, 3 dash-dot, 4 dashed) but the caption defines only one style: 'dashed border = not in the canonical baseline'. Because one style is explicitly made meaningful, a reader can reasonably search for meaning in the dotted and dash-dot styles of boxes 2 and 3 and find none — an unexplained visual variable.
acceptance_test: Either all four boxes share one border style except box 4 (dashed), or the caption/in-figure note states that border styles for boxes 1–3 are decorative and only 'dashed' carries meaning. Re-render and confirm no undefined border style appears.
verdict_evidence: P1 variant of the same defect: the page does show three non-solid borders (solid/dotted/dash-dot/dashed, verified at 2x) with only 'dashed' defined, but boxes 2 and 3 are visibly distinct from box 4's long dashes, so the figure does not literally assert that state management and reuse are outside the baseline - severity is P3, not P1.
fix_instruction: Apply the single-channel fix (solid on 1-3, dashed on 4 only, or an explicit baseline tag on box 4) and re-render; do not redraw the figure around a P1-level contradiction that is not on the page.

quoted_clause: FIGURE 11.3 — host-boundary encoding, case A vs case B
observed: The visual device that encodes 'host' is inconsistent between the two cases, which undercuts the figure's central contrast (one NVLink domain vs across hosts). Case A's two stage boxes sit inside a single light-gray enclosure labelled '8× H100 host' at the top, so the reader sees that both stages share one host. Case B has no equivalent enclosure: '8× H100 host' appears as a line of text inside each colored stage box, so the reader must infer the host boundary from text. The second line of each stage box also carries different semantics in the two cases ('4 GPUs' in A, '8× H100 host' in B), so the same slot means 'GPU count' on the left and 'host descriptor' on the right.
acceptance_test: Apply the same host-boundary device in both cases (e.g. a light-gray enclosure around each host, with the fabric link drawn crossing between two enclosures), and make the second line of every stage box mean the same thing (GPU count). Acceptance: a reader can state, from the geometry alone, that case A's stages share one host and case B's do not.
verdict_evidence: p.213: case A wraps both stage boxes in one light-grey enclosure labelled '8× H100 host', and each box's second line reads '4 GPUs'; case B has no enclosure at all, and its second-line slot instead reads '8× H100 host' in each box - so the host-boundary device and the meaning of the same text slot both differ between the two cases the figure is comparing.
fix_instruction: Give case B the same device as case A - a light-grey enclosure around each host (two enclosures, with the fabric link crossing between them) - and make the second line of every stage box mean the same thing (GPU count / partition), e.g. '4 GPUs' + '4 GPUs' in A and '8 GPUs prefill' + '8 GPUs decode' in B; re-render fig-11-1103 and check the host boundary reads from geometry alone.

quoted_clause: none on this page — footnote 1 (non-figure observation recorded during the page inspection)
observed: Footnote 1 appears to begin mid-URL: the first line starts with a bare commit hash ('a1966e155d8b7508a4947e53cca1d2464f960038/docs/docs/supported-models/diffusion_language_models.mdx') with no scheme or host, and the following lines are a list of repository paths separated by '·'. acceptance_test: Restore the full URL (scheme, host, and path) for every cited file, or replace the path list with a single resolvable repository permalink pinned to the stated commit hash. Acceptance: every URL in the footnote resolves when copied from the printed page.

quoted_clause: Figure 11.4 — in-figure legend (subtitle under 'Device visibility is not a validated serving path')
observed: The in-figure legend 'Solid: dependencies. Dashed: qualify the complete path.' does not account for the dashed column enclosures. Under an arrow-only reading (parallel to 'Solid: dependencies', which covers only solid arrows), the dashed box around each column has no legend entry at all; under an all-dashed reading, the enclosure is misdescribed, because the enclosure groups/marks a complete path and does not 'qualify' anything — only the dashed arrows submit the path to the gate. A reader decoding the figure from its own legend cannot determine what the dashed box means and must be rescued by the caption ('dashed enclosure = complete path').
acceptance_test: Legend distinguishes the two dashed elements, e.g. 'Solid: dependencies within a path. Dashed box: complete path. Dashed arrow: path submitted to the gate.'; re-rendered figure shows no overlap, clipping, or caption reflow after the edit.
verdict_evidence: p.217 figure: three tall dashed rectangles, one per column, plus three dashed arrows into the red gate, but the only in-figure legend is 'Solid: dependencies. Dashed: qualify the complete path.' - one dashed clause for two different dashed elements, and 'qualify' describes the arrows, not the enclosures (which the caption calls 'complete path').
fix_instruction: Split the in-figure subtitle into three matching clauses, e.g. 'Solid arrows: dependencies within a path. Dashed box: complete path per column. Dashed arrow: path submitted to the qualification gate.'; re-render fig-11-backend-paths and confirm no overlap or caption reflow.
